nodes.label: Cross-tenant rental event stream monitoring
Tenant readiness board (which tenants are not fully live)
The single seam: readiness verdict is snapshotted onto the rental at creation
Design stance: passive monitor, never a gate on rental creation
Capture rental creation with a Postgres trigger instead of app code
Rationale: rentals are inserted from 7+ paths with no shared chokepoint, so only Postgres is unbypassable
rentals.creation_context — frozen integration-mode snapshot at rental creation
rentals.health_severity — computed ok/warning/critical verdict
Rationale: snapshot is written synchronously in-DB so the audit survives email/delivery failure
v_tenant_readiness SQL view — per-integration live/test status per tenant
Rationale: readiness is a view, not a table — nothing to keep in sync, and super admins bypass RLS
Per-integration live-ready rules (Stripe, BoldSign, Bonzah, Subscription, Modives)
"Production tenant" heuristic — live-mode active subscription decides critical vs warning
Per-rental severity ladder (critical / warning / ok) and extra alarm signals
Cheap extra signals: first-ever rental milestone and $0 / no-payment-captured flag
Per-rental verdict email with severity in the subject line
platform-rental-notify edge function (JWT-less, pg_net driven)
pg_net shared-secret header as the auth posture for the JWT-less notify function
Planned scaling exit: real-time email for critical only, roll ok/warning into a daily digest
Super-admin unified cross-tenant rentals tab
Monitoring screens must reuse the portal design system (flat borders, indigo, DM Sans)
Decision: defer the platform_notifications delivery log to v2 — the snapshot already records what happened
Phased build order — migration, notify function, readiness board, unified tab, polish
Open questions blocking the plan (recipients, Bonzah in-use signal, log table, nav placement)
rentals table (monitoring: creation_context + health_severity columns)
tenants table (per-integration mode columns read by the readiness verdict)
tenant_subscriptions table (readiness: status + stripe mode)
Stripe Connect production go-live checklist
Platform/marketplace with Express connected accounts
Production Stripe secrets live in Supabase (STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, STRIPE_CONNECT_WEBHOOK_SECRET)
Rationale: server-side Stripe runs in edge functions, so STRIPE_SECRET_KEY is never needed in Vercel
Production webhook endpoint registration (Connect + payments) and signing secrets
stripe-connect-webhook — account.updated / account.application.deauthorized
stripe-webhook — checkout/payment_intent lifecycle events
Onboarding redirect origin falls back to https://portal.drive-247.com
Connect branding for connected accounts (name, icon, brand colour)
Connected-account payout schedule and minimum payout
Production monitoring surfaces: Stripe dashboard, edge-function logs, failure alerts
Production troubleshooting: payments not reaching connected account; onboarding links expire after 24h
Stripe Connect end-to-end test scenario matrix
Prerequisite: two test-mode Stripe accounts (platform + tenant) and the standard test cards
Test: create a tenant's connected account and confirm payouts enabled
Automated payment mode: charge transfers straight to the tenant's connected account
Manual-approval mode: card hold (requires_capture) then staff capture activates the rental
Pre-auth rejection releases the hold and cancels payment + rental with no money moved
Refunds use reverse_transfer, pulling money back out of the tenant's Stripe balance
Partial refund path (refund_amount + "Partial Refund" payment status)
Scheduled refund processed later by a cron job (refund_status scheduled → completed)
Tenants without Stripe Connect cannot create a checkout session at all
create-connected-account edge function
get-connect-onboarding-link edge function
create-checkout-session edge function (tenant resolved via x-tenant-slug)
Stripe CLI --forward-connect-to for local Connect webhook testing
tenants table (Stripe Connect columns: stripe_account_id, stripe_onboarding_complete, stripe_account_status)
payments table (status, capture_status, refund_status, stripe_payment_intent_id, stripe_refund_id)
Migration off the ex-partner "Cortek US" Stripe account onto a self-owned account
CLAUDE / YOU / SKIP task-ownership labelling convention for the migration
Decision: the new platform account is UAE-domiciled
Gotcha: Connect is not self-serve in UAE and US-based operators cannot onboard to a UAE platform
Config-identical twin: blueprint-export the old account, recreate products/prices/coupons by API
All four webhook endpoints must be re-registered on the new account for fresh signing secrets
tenants.stripe_platform_account ('uk' | 'ae') — per-tenant platform-account routing
Extend _shared/stripe-client.ts to resolve keys/secrets by (mode, account)
One webhook URL serves both platform accounts by verifying against both signing secrets
The _AE Supabase secret family (live/test secret, publishable, webhook, connect, subscription)
Per-tenant cutover: PAN copy, recreate subscription, re-onboard Connect, flip the routing flag
Constraint: history, balance and payouts always stay on the old account; operators need fresh KYC/bank
Retire the old account and drop the 'uk' branch from routing code
Two-provider Finance Sync module (Xero + Zoho Books)
Why: operators lose 6–10 hours/month re-keying, and reconciled finance is a stickiness/pricing lever
Provider priority: Xero first, Zoho Books second, QuickBooks Online out of scope
Principle: Drive247 is the only place financial events are born; sync is one-way push
Principle: provider-agnostic from day one — business logic never touches a vendor SDK
Rationale: financial_events is a bridge so operational tables stay untouched and accounting stays decoupled
Principle: idempotent, eventually consistent — unique external ref + state machine + backoff
Principle: every token, job and log entry is namespaced by tenant_id
Gotcha: Xero rotates the refresh token on every refresh and the new one must be persisted
Zoho multi-region data centres — region chosen at connect and baked into every URL
Structural divergence: Xero TaxType enum codes vs Zoho per-org tax UUIDs
Risk: live Xero/Zoho org logins and plaintext passwords are committed inside this repo doc
accounting_connections table — per-tenant per-provider OAuth connection
financial_events table — the internal accounting ledger
financial_event_sync_state table — one row per event per provider
accounting_account_mappings table — event type → provider account/tax code
accounting_contact_links table — customer → provider contact de-duplication
OAuth tokens excluded from client SELECT — expose accounting_connections_public view instead
Server-managed OAuth state: the redirect carries only a nonce, tenant_id is looked up server-side
oauth_state table — short-lived nonce → tenant_id lookup for OAuth callbacks
refresh-accounting-tokens cron — refreshes tokens 15 min before expiry, expires the connection after 3 x 4xx
AccountingProvider interface (upsertContact / createInvoice / recordPayment / createCreditNote)
xero-client.ts — Xero implementation of AccountingProvider
zoho-client.ts — Zoho Books implementation of AccountingProvider (raw HTTP, no SDK)
factory.ts getProvider(tenant_id, provider) — resolves connection, refreshes token, returns client
Gotcha: Zoho has no idempotency header, so writes are guarded by a pre-write existence check
Canonical Drive247-event → Xero/Zoho-action mapping
Rule: pre-auth holds never sync — only captured deposits become book entries
Shipped out-of-box account/tax defaults tuned for a car-rental chart of accounts
One invoice per rental until close/extension/void — matches how a human bookkeeper works
enqueue-financial-event — writes the ledger row plus its initial per-provider sync state
process-accounting-sync worker — batched FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED drain of pending sync rows
Retry backoff 1m/5m/30m/2h/12h then dead-letter (manual retry only)
Account & tax mapping UI (mandatory on first connect, pre-filled with rental-business defaults)
Sync log page and failed-row detail drawer with likely-fix guidance
Per-rental accounting sync badges on the rental detail page
Vehicle Profitability dashboard — revenue/expense/ROI per vehicle from the internal ledger
Opt-in historical backfill — auto-syncing history would create thousands of duplicate invoices
backfill_jobs table — async historical sync job tracking
Provider rate-limit headroom (Xero 50/min of 60, Zoho 80/min, 100 events per tick)
Sync state machine pending → syncing → synced / failed, plus manual skipped
Error classification (transient / auth / validation / duplicate / unknown) decides retry and visibility
Expired connection / >24h failing sync raises a warning row in the existing reminders table
Phase 2: provider webhooks read paid status back (Xero signed endpoint, Zoho per-org workflow rules)
Testing strategy: manual per-provider matrix, mocked unit tests, nightly Xero smoke test
Six-sprint build sequence (34 working days) from ledger foundation to Zoho parity
Finance-sync environment variables (client ids/secrets, DC default, batch size, rate limits)
